openpinn_plate.problem_text:
Plate with circular hole, 2D plane-stress linear elasticity (agent-assisted PINN workflow demonstration, Sec. 5.3).
Geometry: Square plate [0,2]^2 m with a central circular hole of radius 0.25 m centered at (1,1) m; 2D plane stress
Material: Isotropic linear elastic, plane stress, E = 210 GPa, nu = 0.3 (linear elasticity, not hyperelastic)
Boundary conditions: Left edge fixed (taken as ux = uy = 0; components not spelled out); top and bottom outer edges and the hole boundary traction-free; right edge carries the applied traction
Loading: Uniform uniaxial traction of 1 MPa on the right edge (assumed normal/x-direction tension; sign and direction not stated explicitly)
Discretisation in the paper: FEM reference on a probe mesh with h = 0.025 (m); element type, element count and FE code not stated
Features: Corners (0,0) and (0,2) where the fixed left edge meets the traction-free bottom/top edges: stress singularity in the continuum problem (relevant to pointwise stress and the stress relative L2 near those corners); Smooth circular hole of radius 0.25 m: finite stress concentration, not a singularity.
Question: which of these quantities can serve as trustworthy reference values: FEM displacement magnitude (Order of magnitude of FEM reference displacements); SI Adam PINN displacement relative L2 error (Relative L2 error of PINN displacement (width-64 depth-4 MLP, 10000 Adam steps, SI units, seed 0) vs FEM on probe mesh); SI Adam final total loss (Final PINN total training loss, SI units; falls ~1.6% from initial value); SI Adam PDE residual RMSE (RMSE of strong-form equilibrium residual; traction-boundary RMSEs of order 10^10); Nondimensional Adam displacement relative L2 error (3 seeds) (Relative L2 displacement error vs held-out FEM probe mesh h = 0.025, scales L = 1 m, S = 10^6 Pa, U = SL/E, 10000 Adam steps); Final L-BFGS seed-0 displacement relative L2 error (Relative L2 displacement error after 260 fixed-batch L-BFGS steps (2048 interior, 512 boundary points), vs FEM probe mesh and shifted held-out probe set); Final L-BFGS seed-0 stress relative L2 error (Relative L2 stress error vs FEM); Nondimensional x-momentum residual RMSE (seed 0) (RMSE of nondimensional x-momentum residual, Adam vs L-BFGS); Final L-BFGS displacement relative L2 error, seeds 1 and 2 (Relative L2 displacement error vs FEM probe mesh)?

card.title: Open-hole composite lamina (AS4/3501-6, plane stress, elliptical planform with central hole, fibres at 15°)

geometry.value: 2D plane-stress unidirectional lamina with an elliptical planform (semi-axes 50 mm and 10 mm), thickness 1 mm, and a central circular hole of radius 3 mm. Fibres are at 15° to the long axis.
geometry.quote: has an elliptical planform with semi-axes 50 mm and 10 mm, thickness 1 mm and a central hole of radius 3 mm

material.value: AS4/3501-6 lamina. The reference law ψref is linear orthotropic with the moduli of [49] (World-Wide Failure Exercise); the moduli are not given in this section. Synthetic data come from a nonlinear law ψ† fitted to the shear and transverse-compression curves of [49]; its nonlinear part is 40% of the shear strain at failure. The unknown energy ψ(e11,e22,γ12) is restricted to a Sobolev ball of radius K = 64.156 on the strain box Ωc and discretised with polynomials of total degree ≤14 (dimension 680).
material.quote: The reference ψref is the linear orthotropic law with the moduli of [49].

boundary_conditions.value: Pure traction problem with a self-balanced load. Three displacement components at the hole are fixed to remove rigid-body motions. The section does not say which nodes or components are fixed.
boundary_conditions.quote: three displacement components at the hole are fixed to remove the rigid motions of the balanced load

loading.value: Boundary tractions of a homogeneous uniaxial stress along the long axis, with resultant P. Loads are given relative to PD = 1792 N, the load at which the plate with law ψ† first reaches the boundary of Ωc. Results are reported at 0.6PD, 0.7PD and 0.8PD. The certificate is at 0.3PD (537.6 N).
loading.quote: The boundary tractions are those of a homogeneous uniaxial stress along the long axis with resultant P

discretisation.value: 4096 isoparametric quadratic (6-node) triangles on a mapped mesh: 64 divisions around the hole and 32 radially, graded towards the hole, 8320 nodes. A 7-point degree-5 quadrature rule gives 28 672 quadrature points. Strains are also sampled at 9 points per element edge on the hole.
discretisation.quote: The plate is discretised by 4096 isoparametric quadratic triangles on a mapped mesh with 64 divisions around the hole and 32 radially, graded towards the hole (8320 nodes)

reference.quote: these come from one computational chain and have not been reproduced by an independent implementation

qois.name: secant compliance (range width)
qois.definition: Width of the first-order range of the secant compliance over the data-consistent set at 0.6PD, in % of the value. Finite-amplitude end points: 6.927e-5 and 7.153e-5 mm/N, against linear 6.925e-5 and 7.148e-5 mm/N.
qois.quote: The secant compliance is predicted within a range of 6.2% without and 3.2% with the convexity condition

qois.name: mean shear strain, hole zone (range width)
qois.definition: Width of the first-order range of the mean shear strain in the zone around the hole at 0.6PD, in % of the value.

qois.name: mean transverse strain, hole zone (range width)
qois.definition: Width of the first-order range of the mean transverse strain in the hole zone at 0.6PD, in % of the value.
qois.quote: The mean transverse strain in the zone around the hole has a range larger than its value.

qois.name: mean shear strain, far field (range width)
qois.definition: Width of the first-order range of the mean far-field shear strain at 0.6PD, in % of the value.

qois.name: worst-case usage of strain domain Ωc
qois.definition: Largest ratio, over the fibre, of any strain component at any point of the plate to its bound in Ωc (first order). The binding state is the transverse strain at the hole edge.
qois.reported_value: reaches 1 at 0.70PD; 1.29 at 0.8PD; 1.15 with an added 15° coupon; 0.84 with an added 40° coupon
qois.quote: At 0.8PD the usage is 1.29 and the prediction is not valid.

qois.name: certified gate margin at 0.3PD
qois.definition: Smallest certified excess of the capacity term over the residual bound in the sum-of-squares certificates, across 43 pieces on 8 parent boxes of one declared cell.
qois.reported_value: all 43 pieces accepted; smallest margins range from 4.52e-7 to 3.60e-5
qois.quote: All 43 pieces are accepted with positive margin.

singular_features.description: The circular hole (radius 3 mm) is smooth, so it gives a finite stress and strain concentration, not a singularity. The binding transverse strain occurs at the hole edge.
singular_features.quote: the binding state is the transverse strain at the hole edge

singular_features.description: Point constraints (three displacement components fixed at the hole) remove rigid-body motion under a self-balanced load. Ideally the reactions are zero, so no point-load singularity is expected.
singular_features.quote: three displacement components at the hole are fixed to remove the rigid motions of the balanced load

not_stated: Numerical values of the orthotropic moduli of AS4/3501-6 (taken from [49])
Functional form and parameters of the nonlinear data law ψ† (fitted to curves of [49])
Which nodes and displacement components are fixed at the hole
FE mesh-convergence study for the plate model (only the polynomial degree of the law space is varied, and it has not converged at degree 14)
Nonlinear solver type and tolerances for the state solves
Exact extent of the 'hole zone' and 'far field' averaging regions
Absolute values of the QoIs other than compliance (only range widths in % are given)

mean transverse strain, hole zone (range width)
mean shear strain, far field (range width)
worst-case usage of strain domain Ωc

'certified gate margin at 0.3PD' (other): no rule class recognises this kind
needs: reference not verified: a refinement family (and strategies) is needed before its values can be used to measure surrogate errors
no independent code: cross-check with a second solver
pointwise peaks: check boundedness (finite-radius concentration or singularity)

The unknown energy ψ(e11,e22,γ12) is restricted to a Sobolev ball of radius K = 64.156 on the strain box Ωc and discretised with polynomials of total degree ≤14 (dimension 680).
